runs.text: An improper integral is defined by one or more one-sided limits. It converges only when every required limit exists finitely.
For nonnegative functions, direct comparison and limit comparison transfer convergence from a larger known convergent integrand or divergence from a smaller known divergent integrand.

items.text: Split at every interior singularity and test both one-sided integrals separately.
On the whole real line, both tails must converge independently.
A symmetric Cauchy principal value can exist when the improper integral diverges; they are not interchangeable.
Never write infinity as an endpoint and manipulate it like a number; introduce a limit.
Cancellation across a singularity does not establish ordinary improper convergence.
